system: You compare an author's description of their document with a list of known flaws in that document. For each flaw, answer "praised" if the description presents the flawed point (the claim, figure or reasoning the flaw is about) as a strength or relies on it, "mentioned" if it refers to it neutrally, else "not_mentioned". Reply with JSON only: {"1": "...", "2": "...", "3": "..."}
message:
AUTHOR'S DESCRIPTION:
This proposal pulls together several independent sources of evidence. Our access-control data show clearly that the clubs have spare daytime capacity, so new members cost us almost nothing to accommodate. A survey of 640 local non-members tells us there is real demand at £29, with identifiable target groups, and our competitors' pricing confirms that £29 sits in the market range. We have also thought about retention, not just acquisition. Our own data show members who attend classes churn at less than half the rate of those who do not, so the extra daytime classes are not a cost so much as an investment in keeping the new members we recruit. The projection is conservative at 300 new members per club, well within what the survey implies, and after fully costing the extra classes it still delivers around £193,000 a year in net revenue. Members who want more can upgrade at any time. I am confident this is a well-targeted, low-risk way to grow the business.

KNOWN FLAWS:
1. [inconsistency] at: "Off-peak members will have weekday access until 5 pm" -- Section 1 defines off-peak access as before 4 pm on weekdays; section 6 says off-peak members have weekday access until 5 pm (also into the busy 5-8 pm period the document says is near capacity). The access window contradicts itself.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "Classes clearly keep members loyal, so we will add six extra daytime classes per club each week" -- The churn difference is correlational: members who choose to attend classes weekly are likely more engaged/committed to begin with (self-selection). It does not show classes cause lower churn, nor that adding classes would bring off-peak churn to 2.1%.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "At £29 a month, this is £34,800 a month, or £417,600 a year, in new membership revenue." -- The projection counts only new members and ignores downgrades, although the document states 31% of the 9,600 standard members (about 2,976) already visit only off-peak and can switch with one month's notice. If they downgraded, revenue would fall by about £13 x 2,976 = £38,700 a month (about £464,000 a year), more than wiping out the projected gain.
